solution.name: Abandoned cart SMS
solution.metaTitle: Abandoned cart SMS on your own account
solution.metaDescription: Add a single recovery text to your abandoned checkout sequence. You keep your own SMS account and API key, and set the send delay yourself.
solution.lede: Text is the channel people actually read. But it is also the channel where getting it wrong is expensive — which is why the text here is a single, timed reminder about one abandoned checkout, sent through an account you already own.

p: The SMS channel sends one recovery message per abandoned checkout. It is not a broadcast tool and there is no list to upload: the recipient is a customer who was already at the payment step in your store.
That constraint is deliberate. A recovery sequence that texts someone five times is a sequence you will switch off within a week — and by then it has already cost you the customer.

The text channel connects to your existing SMS account with an API key. You keep your provider relationship, your negotiated rate, your sender identities and your invoice. The platform does not resell message volume and does not mark up your bill.

In practice that means the regulatory work stays where it belongs: sender registration, local consent rules and the limits your provider grants are all on your side. We route the message and log the send; we do not file or guarantee the rest.

sections.h: The delay is yours to set
p: The text has its own send delay, independent from the email sequence. That lets you run the two channels in a deliberate order — email first and a text only for the checkouts that are still open, or the reverse — instead of firing everything at the same minute.
bullets: Own send delay, independent of the email sequence
One recovery message per abandoned checkout
Send log kept alongside the email results

p: A text that arrives while the customer is still on their phone reads as helpful. The same text an hour later reads as tracking. Set the delay against your own buying cycle and watch recovered orders — not send volume — to decide whether it was right.

Messaging consent and opt-out compliance in the countries you text, sender ID and number registration, the quotas and rate limits your provider grants, and the accuracy of the message you write. These are between you and your provider.

faq.q: Do I have to use my own SMS provider?
faq.a: Yes. The channel is bring-your-own-account: you connect an existing SMS account with an API key. That keeps your rate, your sender identity and your invoice where they already are.

faq.q: Can I send marketing campaigns through this channel?
faq.a: No. It exists for one thing: a single recovery message for an abandoned checkout. There is no list import and no broadcast feature.

faq.q: Can I turn the text channel off and keep emails?
faq.a: Yes — the two channels are independent. Run email alone, text alone, or both with different delays.
